en: The national flower, Sampaguita, blooms best in tropical climates and its sweet scent is strongest at night to attract pollinating moths.
The Narra tree, our national tree, drops its bright yellow flowers in clusters during the dry season to attract wind and insect pollinators.
The Philippine Eagle builds the largest nest of any bird of prey, using sturdy branches high in the canopy of Mindanao's dipterocarp forests.
The carabao, our national animal, wallows in mud to cool its body and protect its sensitive skin from the harsh tropical sun.
During the Pahiyas Festival, Lucban locals decorate their homes with kiping, which are leaf-shaped wafers made from ground rice dyed with natural plant extracts.
The Ifugao built the Banaue Rice Terraces by carving steps into the mountains and using an ancient stone irrigation system to channel mountain springs.
National Scientist Ramon Barba discovered that spraying mango trees with potassium nitrate solution induces flowering even during the dry season.
The perfectly symmetrical cone of Mayon Volcano is a visible geological feature formed by repeated layers of cooled lava and volcanic ash.
National Scientist Angel Alcala established marine sanctuaries in the Visayas, where protecting coral reefs visibly increases the number of fish swimming in nearby waters.
The South Sea pearl, our national gem, forms inside the Pinctada maxima oyster when a microscopic irritant gets trapped beneath its shell layers.
T'boli weavers create the T'nalak cloth by extracting abaca fibers from local plants and dyeing them with natural roots and leaves found in their environment.
The tamaraw, our national mammal, has distinct V-shaped horns and a white facial stripe that help it navigate the dense, dark grasslands of Mindoro.
